name: Thalamus (context envelope)
contextNote: Envelope/block tag for the thalamus silhouette on sagittal and coronal plates and in the 3D scene; not a nucleus record (see the 14 individual thalamic nucleus records).

name: Internal medullary lamina
contextNote: Context record: white-matter lamina tagged on plate-thalamus-mid and plate-coronal-thalamus; not a functional nucleus — see the individual thalamic nucleus records.

name: Hypothalamus (context envelope)

name: Pineal body (context silhouette)
contextNote: Envelope/context-surface record: the GLB silhouette ctx-pineal in src/assets/anatomy/anatomy-manifest.json is its 3D body (SceneLayers envelope slot env-pineal), and its canonical-space extent below is that baked bbox — note that the baked body is markedly larger than the endocrine gland it names, so it reads as an epithalamic block rather than a gland. Distinct from nuc-pineal-gland, which is the endocrine/clinical record; no plate carries this tag.

name: Fields of Forel (H1/H2)
contextNote: Schematic context record for the H1/H2 white-matter regions around zona incerta. The source textbook labels the convergence area prerubral field H; numerical variants such as H3 are not used here. This silhouette is not a validated stereotactic target.

name: Corpus callosum (context)
contextNote: Context silhouette for the sagittal plate and 3D scene roof; not a diencephalic structure (hemisphere context).

name: Internal capsule (context)
contextNote: Context silhouette on plate-thalamus-mid and plate-coronal-thalamus; see also the subthalamus records for the pallidal (H1/H2) fasciculi looping through it.

name: Lentiform nucleus (context silhouette)
contextNote: Context silhouette of the lentiform (putamen + globus pallidus) mass on plate-thalamus-mid and plate-coronal-thalamus. v19 (audit FAC-DI-008): the old sentence "basal-ganglia detail is out of scope for v1" was stale — v7/v8 shipped the detail it deferred, as the nucleus records nuc-putamen, nuc-globus-pallidus-internus, nuc-globus-pallidus-externus, nuc-caudate-head, nuc-caudate-body, nuc-caudate-tail, nuc-ventral-striatum and nuc-accumbens, and the capsule segments tract-internal-capsule-anterior-limb/-genu/-posterior-limb. This record is the silhouette that CONTAINS them; use the nucleus records for content.

name: CN III Oculomotor nerve
contextNote: This nerve is displayed as an authored course tube, not a segmented specimen. The central nuclear crossing pattern differs from the ipsilateral targets of the peripheral nerve: superior-rectus nuclear fibers cross, and levator control is bilateral. Coordinates, tube thickness and orbital waypoints are conceptual.

name: CN IV Trochlear nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic course. Pre-crossing nuclear/fascicular injury and post-crossing nerve injury have different laterality; a single tube cannot certify the intramedullary crossing geometry.

name: CN V Trigeminal nerve
contextNote: The drawn common-root/V3 course does not depict all V1/V2/V3 branches. No root crossing occurs; many second-order trigeminothalamic fibers cross within the brainstem. This is not a second crossing of primary nerve fibers.

name: CN VI Abducens nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic course; the nerve and the nuclear internuclear pathway are distinct. Clival/skull-base/orbital relationships have no registered skull model.

name: CN VII Facial nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic common course; branch-level facial canal and gland pathways are text only. Lesion position determines whether taste, tear/salivary or stapedius deficits accompany facial weakness.

name: CN VIII Vestibulocochlear nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic course represents the common intracranial path, not each inner-ear branch or a validated labyrinth. Sensory nerve central projections and reflex efferents are distinguished.

name: CN IX Glossopharyngeal nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic root/jugular course. The principal parasympathetic source is inferior salivatory nucleus; DMV is a vagal nucleus and is not substituted as IX secretomotor origin.

name: CN X Vagus nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic common nerve; recurrent laryngeal and abdominal branches are not individually reconstructed. The classic cranial-XI root is functionally vagal, separate from spinal XI shoulder fibers.

name: CN XI Accessory nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic course; a medullary surface waypoint does not represent the true spinal motor origin. Upper cervical rootlets and foramen-magnum entry require separate geometry to be anatomically faithful.

name: CN XII Hypoglossal nerve
contextNote: Authored schematic course from medullary exit to canal/tongue; no specimen-segmented canal or tongue reconstruction. Tongue deviation laterality depends on lower versus upper motor neuron injury.

name: Arcuate fasciculus
contextNote: Concept record with no dedicated segmented volume or tractography streamlines. No origin3d, size3d or waypoints are assigned; the cortex/tract descriptions are educational, not patient-specific localization.
